question_text: Which is the correct way to file 'The Bureau of Internal Revenue' in an alphabetical index?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 1
hint_ladder.text: Think about how you'd look up a government agency in a phone book or filing cabinet. Would you search under 'The' or under the main name?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 2
hint_ladder.text: In alphabetical filing, small words like 'The', 'A', and 'An' at the start of a name are ignored. They get moved to the end, separated by a comma.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 3
hint_ladder.text: So for 'The Bureau of Internal Revenue', you take 'The' off the front, put it at the back with a comma, and file under the word that comes next.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 4
hint_ladder.text: The correct filing form is 'Bureau of Internal Revenue, The'. This way, you alphabetize by 'Bureau' — the real first word — not by 'The'.

A.text: This is exactly right. You moved 'The' to the end after a comma, so the name is filed under 'Bureau'. That's the standard rule for articles at the start of a name.

B.text: This keeps 'The' at the front, which is a common mistake. In filing, 'The' is considered a non-filing word, so it should not be the first thing you alphabetize by. Always drop it to the end.

C.text: This flips the words around too much. You might be thinking of how you'd file a person's last name first, but for organizations, you keep the natural order — just move the article. 'Internal Revenue, Bureau of' is not the correct form here.

D.text: This is scrambled beyond recognition. It looks like you tried to invert the name but went too far. The rule is simple: keep the name in its natural order, and only move the article 'The' to the end.

deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this together. The name is 'The Bureau of Internal Revenue'. In alphabetical filing, small articles like 'The', 'A', and 'An' at the very beginning are treated as non-filing words. They don't help you find anything because almost no one looks up 'The' in a directory. So the trick is to move 'The' to the very end, separated by a comma. That gives you 'Bureau of Internal Revenue, The'. Now you alphabetize by 'Bureau' — the first real, meaningful word. Think of it like this: if you were flipping through a filing cabinet, you'd look under 'B' for Bureau, not under 'T' for The. That's the mental shortcut: always ask yourself, 'What word would I actually search for?' and file by that word instead.
next_time_rule: When you see 'The', 'A', or 'An' at the start of a name, mentally cut it off and paste it at the end with a comma. File by the next real word.
